frozen-dictionary-read-mostly.title: Build read-mostly maps with FrozenDictionary
frozen-dictionary-read-mostly.short: Optimize a dictionary for lookup after its contents stop changing.
frozen-dictionary-read-mostly.summary: FrozenDictionary<TKey,TValue> fixes its contents during construction and is intended for efficient repeated lookup. It fits configuration tables, routing maps, and other data built once and read many times.
frozen-dictionary-read-mostly.why: A normal Dictionary remains mutable. When a map is known to be immutable after setup, converting it to FrozenDictionary also communicates that lifecycle in the code.
frozen-dictionary-read-mostly.tips: Freezing has an up-front cost, so avoid rebuilding frozen dictionaries in short-lived hot paths. Pass an appropriate comparer when key comparison rules matter.

configureawait-library-code.title: Use ConfigureAwait(false) in context-free library code
configureawait-library-code.short: Avoid requiring a captured synchronization context for an await continuation.
configureawait-library-code.summary: ConfigureAwait(false) tells an await that its continuation does not need to resume through the captured synchronization context. It is mainly relevant to reusable library code that does not depend on a UI context.
configureawait-library-code.why: UI application code may need to resume on its UI context, while internal library operations often have no such requirement. Distinguishing the two avoids accidental context dependencies.
configureawait-library-code.tips: Do not add it mechanically everywhere. Decide whether the continuation needs a context and apply a consistent policy within library code.

iasyncdisposable-await-using.title: Dispose IAsyncDisposable with await using
iasyncdisposable-await-using.short: Reliably await asynchronous cleanup when leaving a scope.
iasyncdisposable-await-using.summary: Objects implementing IAsyncDisposable can be declared with await using. When the scope exits, DisposeAsync is awaited so asynchronous cleanup completes before execution continues.
iasyncdisposable-await-using.why: Some resources need asynchronous I/O during cleanup. await using also preserves structured cleanup when an exception leaves the scope.
iasyncdisposable-await-using.tips: Dispose only resources your code owns. A Stream borrowed from a caller may need to remain open, so ownership is still part of the API design.

regex-source-generator.title: Generate regular expressions with GeneratedRegex
regex-source-generator.short: Generate the implementation for a fixed Regex pattern at compile time.
regex-source-generator.summary: GeneratedRegexAttribute on a partial method lets the regular-expression source generator provide the implementation. It gives frequently reused fixed patterns a clear declaration in code.
regex-source-generator.why: Instead of constructing a Regex from the same pattern at runtime, the pattern can be represented as a declaration with a generated reusable implementation.
regex-source-generator.tips: The method and containing type must be partial. GeneratedRegex is for patterns known at compile time, not patterns supplied dynamically by users.

checked-overflow-context.title: Detect integer overflow with checked
checked-overflow-context.short: Prevent out-of-range integer arithmetic from silently wrapping.
checked-overflow-context.summary: In a checked context, supported integral arithmetic and conversions throw OverflowException when the result cannot be represented by the destination type. Use it when exceeding the numeric range is an error.
checked-overflow-context.why: Unchecked integer arithmetic can wrap around, leaving a plausible-looking but incorrect value that hides the original range error.
checked-overflow-context.tips: checked is useful around external input, money, counts, and other calculations where overflow is invalid. Code intentionally relying on wraparound, such as some bit-level algorithms, needs a different choice.
